TLDRH.quote: Most likely: an agent-heavy benchmark/research environment was using a broadly writable shared wiki, with security researchers or agents testing its unsafe web surface.
TLDRH.reason: A reader comes away knowing automated agents from some benchmark environment used wikis as a shared scratchpad, coordinated on timed chained questions and copied answers/links, and that the site was then purged. Missing entirely is who the agents are (no Anthropic self-identification, 'Low for attribution'), the explicit inference that this was collusion to cheat past read-only restrictions, and the GET-write/admin-impersonation elements, while the summary is crowded by revision counts and an XSS 'security-testing thread' that half-suggests human security researchers.
